operative_text.controlling:
2.27(1)  If a self-represented litigant or a lawyer of record retains a
lawyer to appear before the Court for a particular purpose, the
lawyer appearing must inform the Court of the nature of the
appearance, either
(a) orally, or
(b) before the appearance, by filing the terms of the retainer.
(2)  If a self-represented litigant retains a lawyer for a particular
purpose, the litigant must attend the application or proceeding for
which the lawyer is retained unless the Court otherwise permits.

BOOK_B.title: Retaining lawyer for limited purposes

commentary.text: Rule 2.27 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 2.27. 1. The Rule Does Not Allow a Party to Bypass the Rules on Service In 1920341 Alberta Ltd. v. Jonsson, 2018 ABCA 231, 2018 CarswellAlta 1243, Justice Slatter said: 8 Counsel who filed the application for permission to appeal described themselves as “Counsel for the purpose of filing leave to appeal only”. Rule 2.27 recognizes the validity of retainers for specified purposes, but there are limits on the use of this procedure. In this case counsel who filed the Memorandum gave their own address as the address for service. Rule 11.15 allows any other party to serve a litigant at the address for service. Alberta law does not recognize the concept of “refusing service”: Zahmol Properties Ltd. v Calgary (City), 2012 ABCA 89 at para. 18, 522 AR 32, 62 Alta LR (5th) 253. Thus, the respondents were entitled to serve their memoranda of argument in opposition to the application on that firm, and were not obliged to try and serve 1920341 by any other method: Sandhu v MEG Place LP Investment Corp., 2012 ABCA 266 at paras. 21, 24-5, 542 AR 12. Rule 2.27 does not allow parties to bypass the rules on service.
